title: Observability pipeline ingestion debug notes (tracing/metrics/logs) - WIP
content:
Context:
- Started seeing partial telemetry loss over the weekend (2026-02-19 -> 2026-02-20 deploy window). Symptoms: ~25-35% of spans not showing up in traces, metrics ingestion rate down ~12% vs baseline, and log-ingest backlog on kafka topic 'observability-ingest' increased from ~0 -> ~120k in 6 hours then stalled.

High-level timeline (what I saw locally / infra signals):
- 2026-02-19 22:15 UTC: Deploy (ingest-collector v2.14.0) rolled out to prod regions (EU/US).
- 2026-02-20 01:10 UTC: Pager triggered: "Tracing pipeline: span drop rate > 20% (15m)". Alerts also for "metrics ingestion throughput drop".
- 2026-02-20 01:20 UTC: Slack thread OBS-321 started, infra pager engaged.
- 2026-02-20 02:00 UTC: Rollback to v2.13.2 on a canary pool showed partial recovery (drops reduced but not back to baseline).

Repro / quick checks run so far (commands & outputs):
1) Check collector pods and restarts
- kubectl -n observability get pods -l app=ingest-collector -o wide
  --> several pods on node ip-10-0-8-12 showing RESTARTS=3 in last 24h

2) Inspect collector logs (high-volume, filter errors)
- kubectl -n observability logs deploy/ingest-collector -c agent --since=2h | egrep "WARN|ERROR|drop|buffer|decode" | tail -n 200
  Snippets seen:
  - "WARN: dropped 1234 spans due to buffer full (batcher.go:256)"
  - "ERROR: decoding error: unexpected EOF while parsing protobuf (protobuf_decoder.go:112)"
  - "WARN: kafka produce retries exceeded, last error: 503 Service Unavailable"

3) Check kafka topic & consumer lag (kafkactl):
- kafkactl get topic observability-ingest -o json | jq '.partitions[].endOffset'
- kafkactl consumer-group -g ingest-consumers -o wide
  Output: consumer lag jumped to ~120k for partition 3; consumers show steady consumption but occasional stalls with reconnects.

4) Quick curl to collector health & telemetry endpoints
- curl -sS http://ingest-collector.europe.svc.cluster.local:8080/healthz
  -> {"status":"ok","ingest_queue_len":17342,"batcher_active":true}
- curl -sS http://ingest-collector.europe.svc.cluster.local:8080/metrics | grep batcher
  -> batcher_queue_length 17342
  -> batcher_batches_total 1.2e6

5) Reproduce send with a small test payload (python script)
- python tests/send_sample_traces.py --host ingest-collector.europe:8080 --count 10000 --rate 200
  Observed ~12% drop reported by client and collector logs show a mix of decode errors + buffer-full warnings.

6) Node-level metrics for problematic node (kubectl top / node-exporter)
- Node ip-10-0-8-12: memory: 1.8Gi used (limit 2Gi), CPU spiky but <70%. JVM/collector thread-dumps show frequent GC pauses (~200-300ms) and thread blocked on network write.

Experiments/troubleshooting performed (in order):
- 1) Rollback canary to v2.13.2: partial improvement -> suggests change in v2.14.0 is related.
- 2) Increased collector replicas from 6 -> 9 in EU region: ingestion rate improved marginally, consumer lag growth slowed but didn't resolve.
- 3) Reduced batch_size from 1000 -> 200 (config via ConfigMap): small improvement in memory pressure and fewer 'buffer full' drops but decode errors persisted.
- 4) Disabled compressions (gzip) for a short window (to see decode failures): decode errors reduced, which points to either compression/uncompression mismatch or corrupted messages in transit.
- 5) Forced full GC (JVM option tweak) on one replica: memory stabilized but no meaningful change in drop rate.
- 6) Ran tcpdump on one node for collector -> kafka traffic and replayed some captured payloads locally: some messages truncated (tcp retransmits), pointing to potential L7 proxy / MTU issue on host network path.

Error snippets collected (raw):
- "ERROR: decoding error: unexpected EOF while parsing protobuf at offset 834"
- "WARN: dropped 1234 spans due to buffer full (batcher.go:256)"
- "ERROR: kafka produce failed: 503 Service Unavailable (broker-2)"
- "WARN http2: transport: readfrom /10.5.3.21: net/http2: invalid response body"

Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
- A) Message corruption / truncation between collector and kafka (network path / LB / proxy issue) -> explains truncated protobuf + tcp retransmits observed.
- B) Compression mismatch bug introduced in v2.14.0 (compress/decompress flag handling) -> disabling compression reduced decode errors.
- C) Kafka broker under pressure/partial outage returning 503s -> transient backpressure causing buffer-fill and drops.
- D) New sampling/default batching config in v2.14.0 increased per-message size causing occasional exceed of MTU and fragmentation leading to truncation.
- E) Memory GC thrashing on collectors causing delayed writes and fills -> less likely as rolling restart/GC fiddles didn't fix completely.

Important observations to tie hypotheses:
- Disabling compression reduced decode errors (supports B).
- tcpdump shows truncated frames and frequent retransmits to broker IPs (supports A and D).
- Kafka metrics show broker-2 reporting higher CPU and request latency around the window (supports C but not primary).

Immediate mitigation steps taken / suggested (and who did what):
- Rolled back canary in EU (Ava) -> partial improvement.
- Increased replica count and lowered batch size (Marcus) -> reduced bump but not fixed.
- Disabled compression in config map (Priya) -> decoded errors decreased by ~70% in one pod.
- Infra asked to check network path (ticket NET-998 opened to infra) -> pending.

Next debugging steps (actionable):
- 1) Reproduce truncation locally: capture network stream between a collector and a kafka broker, then replay at different MTU sizes to see if fragmentation causes truncation. (Ava + infra)
- 2) Run a controlled canary with compression off and telemetry debug logging enabled across 3 replicas (low impact zone). Collect protobuf bytes for failed messages. (Ava)
- 3) Add boundary checks and message-size logging in collector binary (instrumentation PR): log exact message length and checksum before send so we can tell if corruption happens pre- or post-send. (PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/487)
- 4) Coordinate with Kafka on-call to check broker-2 for disk / NIC errors and controller logs in the exact window (Marcus). (OBS-321)
- 5) Check our LB / sidecar (istio envoy) configs for new connection buffer limits / http2 settings introduced last month (possible interaction with HTTP2 body framing). (Priya)
- 6) If network truncation reproducible, try mtu=1400 on path (or enable TCP segmentation offload) to see effect. (infra)

Metrics / dashboards to watch (links or queries):
- traces.ingest.span_drop_rate (15m)
- collector.batcher.queue_length by pod
- kafka.consumer.lag{group="ingest-consumers"}
- broker.request.latency (broker-2)
- node.network.retransmits / node.if_errors

Open items / questions for infra & platform:
- Are there any recent kernel or CNI changes on the problematic nodes around 2026-02-18 -> 02-19? (possible MTU or TSO/TSO bug)
- Any maintenance on LB / envoy / ALB that might alter http2 framing or close mid-body?
- Can we get tcpdump for the last 24h from the problematic node and from kafka broker-2?

Notes to self / small TODOs:
- Add short script to pull protobuf bytes for failed requests and calc crc32 -> stash to S3 for later analysis.
- Add a Grafana panel to show "compress_enabled" config per deployment revision to quickly check if compression toggled.
- Follow up with infra NET-998 and attach tcpdump samples to OBS-321.

Links & references:
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02OBSERV/threads/p1234567890
- Jira: OBS-321 (ingest partial loss)
- PR with instrumentation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/487

Conclusion / current status:
- Root cause not 100% confirmed. Leading theory: combination of compression bug in v2.14.0 (makes some messages invalid for decoder) + network fragmentation/truncation occurring in some paths (makes a subset of messages fail to reassemble). Kafka broker load may amplify the symptom by producing 503s/backpressure.
- Short term: keep compression disabled for canary until we finish replay/packet-level validation.
- Long term: add stronger message checks (size + checksum), add retry logic that validates before enqueue, and investigate network path to fix fragmentation or MTU mismatch.

If you have time please: run the replay test locally (tests/replay_capture.py) and ping infra for NET-998. I will continue with PR instrumentation and attach sample failing protobufs to OBS-321.

-- Ava
